about: Which library constraints a Learning Goal may select, by owner ruling, with the manipulations its context names evaluated against the knowledge that exists. Ids, citations, statuses and his words only: nothing here is a value, a mapping to an Environmental Manipulation or Affordance Target id, or a candidate pool. Where a goal has an entry, selection draws its constraints from authorizedConstraints and from nothing else (not the wording pool, not the Game Problem's Coverage row), in both pathways. authorizedConstraints null means the record has not yet evaluated which constraints the knowledge justifies: a knowledge gap (NO_AUTHORIZED_CONSTRAINTS), never a fallback. A list (with its finding) is the evaluation; an EMPTY list means none is justified, and under the general principle below the goal is selected with no library constraint. The principle is recorded once, here, and applies to every record alike: no goal is special-cased. ADDED 15 October 2026 (stage H3, his 16 October reply, item 10: 'The decisions above should be interpreted as either: General learning-design principles. Provisional realization choices for the first activity. Existing knowledge relationships that require verification. Genuine implementation or knowledge gaps. Please keep those categories distinct.'): every manipulation and provisional choice names its CATEGORY (what its authority is: PROVISIONAL_REALIZATION_CHOICE, his choice for this activity; EXISTING_KNOWLEDGE_TO_VERIFY, the game form, the context or the session, offered for his verification; GENUINE_GAP, nothing settles it; a GENERAL_PRINCIPLE is recorded once, at the top) beside its STATUS (whether the activity can carry it now). A status of MISSING_KNOWLEDGE or MISSING_CAPABILITY means the activity his rulings ask for needs it and it is not in place; it names the decisions and capabilities (gaps, defined in the record) that would supply it, and the build refuses the goal naming each one rather than build an activity that solves a different problem. existingKnowledge lists what existing knowledge already authorizes for the activity, with its sources. The decision and capability ids (D1-D7, M1-M8) and their one-line descriptions are OUR wording, as put to him; none is his. AMENDED 15 October 2026 (stage K2), narrowly, for his reply filed 17 October 2026: 'The priority remains producing one complete, representative Play Out from the Back activity through the normal generation pathway, without introducing unnecessary architecture or treating this first realization as the canonical version of the Learning Goal.' A record may name ONE provisional realization (provisionalRealization: an id in docs/audits/conformance/stage-b/provisional-realizations.json). That file, not this one, holds his provisional realization choices as contract items in his words; derivation adds them only for the goal whose record names the realization, every one carries the category PROVISIONAL_REALIZATION_CHOICE into the game, and none is canonical knowledge of the context. This record still holds no value: it names the realization, as it names a constraint. AMENDED 15 October 2026 (stage K4), narrowly, for his replies filed 17 and 18 October 2026: the file now records ONE mapping to an Environmental Manipulation, the context-manipulation relationship he asked for and then confirmed (contextManipulationRelationships; 17 October, D6: 'Please authorize this initial numerical asymmetry through the appropriate existing knowledge relationship, rather than hardcoding it to Play Out from the Back.'; 18 October, item 5: 'Goalkeeper Build-Out with Participant Composition.'), his allocation principle once (allocationPrinciple), and, in a record, the adjustments he authorized for that goal's activity, in his words (authorizedAdjustments). An adjustment names a count only where his words do. The starting counts themselves stay in the provisional realization, never here.

libraryConstraintPrinciple.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (called his 16 October reply, to keep it apart from his first 15 October reply), item 1
libraryConstraintPrinciple.principle: A library constraint is not mandatory unless its inclusion is justified by the approved knowledge and intended learning environment.
words: I agree that an activity should not require two to four library constraints simply to satisfy an engine quota.

The game form and its inherent conditions may already create the affordances needed for the Learning Goal. Additional constraints should be selected because they serve a documented learning-design purpose, not because the engine requires a particular number.
However, I want the underlying principle to apply generally:
A library constraint is not mandatory unless its inclusion is justified by the approved knowledge and intended learning environment.

I understand that applying this immediately to every Learning Goal could interrupt existing functionality. We can implement the correction incrementally, but please don't establish Play Out from the Back as a permanent special-case exception.
The engine should continue enforcing structural validity and any genuinely required conditions.
libraryConstraintPrinciple.appliedAs: Every Learning Goal whose authorization record has evaluated its authorized constraints and found none justified (an empty list) is selected with its game form and lenses and no library constraint; derivation, realization and every gate still run on it. Applied incrementally, as his words allow: a goal reaches it only once it has a record, and goals without one keep the vocabulary pool and the two-to-four rule. The lens rule (two or three) is unchanged: his item 1 speaks of library constraints, not lenses.

allocationPrinciple.principle: The important principle is that player allocation should reflect representative numerical relationships, not default to equal outfield numbers regardless of the Learning Goal.
words: In match play, teams building from the back commonly have more players available in their defensive third than the opposition initially commits to pressing.
A building-team numerical advantage is therefore not necessarily an artificial simplification. It can be representative of the actual performance environment.
The important principle is that player allocation should reflect representative numerical relationships, not default to equal outfield numbers regardless of the Learning Goal.
Please authorize this initial numerical asymmetry through the appropriate existing knowledge relationship, rather than hardcoding it to Play Out from the Back.
Please do not assign a goalkeeper an inactive role solely to preserve a symmetrical team structure.
allocationPrinciple.appliedAs: Recorded once, with no goal id, and applied without one. Equal outfield numbers stay the possession game's own knowledge (GF2-14.b): ruling C56 lets that item defer only in a composition where another selected contribution authors the outfield count per team and cites a CONFIRMED relationship below that authorizes the row (back/src/system/derivation/realization-deferral.ts); it is then listed as the alternative. The roster reads per-team counts from such items alone and refuses rather than choose: an allocation that fits no authored count is refused for that session (CONFIGURATION_DOES_NOT_FIT), and authored per-team counts with the equal-numbers requirement still in force are refused (NO_AUTHORIZED_ASYMMETRY). A goalkeeper available and not involved is counted among the outfield players by the roster's availability-is-not-involvement rule (his ruling of 30 September), so no goalkeeper is idled to make the teams symmetric; that is the only reading given to his last sentence, kept to what he said.

ruling: I approve Gain Access as the primary Game Problem for Play Out from the Back, based on the approved Goalkeeper Build-Out context and its scoring condition.

Create Space remains relevant as a potential means of solving the problem, but I agree that we should not assign it as a secondary Game Problem at this stage. Let's retain our existing decision to defer secondary Game Problems.
This resolves the Cycle 8 translation gap for this Learning Goal through the approved context rather than inference from the goal's wording.
One important distinction: approving Gain Access does not automatically authorize the candidate constraints currently derived from vocabulary coverage.
I would prefer that the activity's constraints be selected based on their documented relationship to the approved context, Game Problem, and target affordances.

The context's existing manipulations—starting positions, field dimensions, progression references, defensive numbers, goalkeeper positioning, overloads, and support spacing—are appropriate candidates for evaluation. However, they should not automatically become selected constraints simply because they appear in that list.
Please identify the smallest set of authorized manipulations needed to create a representative build-out problem, and flag any missing knowledge rather than filling gaps through inference.
authorizations.authorizedConstraintsFinding: No library constraint has a documented relationship to Goalkeeper Build-Out (RPC-001), Gain Access (GP-005) or this goal's affordances. RPC-001's relationships in rpc-library.rc1.json reach only the game archetype, Game Problem, game form, Learning Goal and scoring event libraries, and it has no manipulation property; its affordance targets RPC-MAP-091..096 are DEFERRED by Christian on 13 September 2026 ('canonical Affordance Target ids are not to be inferred to reach runtime'); every Soccer Module realization row has universal_concept_id and primary_game_problem_ids null; the Coverage rows and the wording pools were both derived by the parser. Finding of 15 October 2026 (stage G1), for his review: it names no constraint as authorized.

provisionalChoices.choice: The first Play Out from the Back activity carries no selected library constraint (Option A): its environment is the game form, the approved context and what he authorizes.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 1
provisionalChoices.words: Please proceed with Option A for Play Out from the Back.
provisionalChoices.note: Not the mechanism: selection commits no constraint here because the authorized set is evaluated and empty, under the general principle recorded once at the top of this file. This entry records that he chose it for this activity, and that it is provisional.

provisionalChoices.choice: An asymmetrical build-out-versus-press structure: one team builds out, the other presses to prevent progression, regain possession and exploit the regain, and the teams exchange roles over successive episodes or blocks.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 2
provisionalChoices.words: For the first demonstration, I favor an asymmetrical game structure. One team begins by building out from its goalkeeper or a controlled defensive restart. The opposing team attempts to prevent progression, regain possession, and exploit the regain. The teams exchange roles over successive episodes or blocks so both experience the Learning Goal. This is a provisional realization choice, not a universal requirement for Play Out from the Back.
provisionalChoices.note: Nothing in the knowledge attaches a fact to one team by its role for a block, and nothing represents blocks or exchanging roles (measured 15 October 2026: the roster gives every team one equal count, and a team-specific selector is refused as not settled). Whether roles swap by block or by episode is decision D2; the pressing team's objective and how it is named (his 9.6, revised by us) wait on his acknowledgement, D7. His item 2 also: 'Symmetrical, continuous games should remain legitimate alternatives when they create the appropriate learning environment.'

provisionalChoices.choice: An intermediate progression reference or target for the build-out, not a distant terminal end zone; no mandated midfield and no universal depth.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 4
provisionalChoices.words: I therefore favor an intermediate progression reference or target over a distant terminal end zone for this first activity.
provisionalChoices.note: The choice stands; WHERE the target sits is the gap recorded on 'progression references' below (D3). It supersedes the far-end 5 m prototype of his 15 October item 2.

provisionalChoices.choice: After a defensive regain, the pressing team plays for a target area toward a higher attacking player or attacking space, reached by controlled entry; not, for now, a goalkeeper-defended goal.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 5
provisionalChoices.words: After considering the available targets, I favor a target area representing successful progression toward a higher attacking player or attacking space for the first demonstration. This target would be available following a defensive regain. Success should be possible through controlled entry, either by carrying the ball or by passing to a teammate who receives under control.
provisionalChoices.note: Each team already has its own target in a different place (ruling C42), so the area itself is representable; its depth is the gap on 'progression references' below (D3), and whether it is live throughout the pressing team's block is part of D7. Item 5 also refuses a rule requiring a teammate to receive inside the target after a regain there, and asks for no transition window, pass sequence, timing condition or automatic high-regain bonus; none is recorded. A target player, small goal or goalkeeper-defended goal stays an alternative, not excluded: alongside a zone for the other team it would need a scoring event kind per team, which one primary scoring event per game (SD-06) does not allow today.

provisionalChoices.choice: A new build-out episode begins with a goalkeeper or controlled defensive restart once the previous episode has meaningfully concluded, without interrupting a promising attack; after a score play stops and restarts, at a location the coach selects.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 6 and 6.ii
provisionalChoices.words: For this first activity, I favor returning to a goalkeeper or controlled defensive restart when an episode has meaningfully concluded. However, the activity should not interrupt a promising attacking or counterattacking opportunity simply because the initial build-out objective has been achieved. … After a score: Yes, play stops and restarts. The coach can select an appropriate authorized restart location, consistent with the intended build-out situation.
provisionalChoices.note: Nothing in the knowledge means 'the episode has concluded' (the trigger list is closed: a score, the ball going out, a change of possession, a completed pass and the like), and the game holds no start or score transition element, so no build-out episode can begin (measured 15 October 2026: GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE). The restart location as the coach's choice extends what a coach decides and needs his ruling (D5, M3). Whether reaching the progression target is a score that stops play is D1: his 6.ii answered a question we had framed around the far-end zone. The possession game's ordinary out-of-play rule is not the preferred restart here (6.iii). Carried since 15 October 2026 (stage K5), on his 17 October D1, D5, M3 and M4 and his 18 October items 2 and 4: A01-R1's start, after-score and coach-judged conclusion transitions stop and restart play, are awarded to the team holding the building role and taken by its goalkeeper from the feet at a location the coach chooses (A01-R1-T1-1..3, T6-1, T7-1, T2-1, T3-1, T4-1, T5-1); the coach-judged conclusion is the trigger registered for his M4 (register version 12); ball out is an ordinary restart partitioned by who touched it last - a throw-in on the touchline, the coach's method on the end line - that continues the episode off the pressing team and ends the build-out off the building team (A01-R1-T1-4..7 and their items); and the build-out begin condition is typed in his acknowledged wording (ruling C58), so GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE passes in both blocks with one awardee. That the end-line location is the coach's too, and who takes an end-line restart, are our readings put to him for a one-line confirmation. Until stage K5 this was MISSING_CAPABILITY, waiting on D1, D5, M3 and M4.

provisionalChoices.choice: The third build-out origin described in RC1.1 stays outside the first implementation, its workbook omission recorded for reconciliation.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 6
provisionalChoices.words: The third build-out origin described in RC1.1 can remain outside the first implementation, as you recommend, while its workbook omission is recorded for reconciliation.

existingKnowledge.what: Two opposed teams, the opposition live and able to deny, redirect or reverse progression.
Each team attacks its own target, the two targets in different places.
One scoring event kind serves both targets, and the context approves a zone entered or a line crossed.
existingKnowledge.note: The vocabulary definition of a zone being entered is our drafting, not his words; his item 5 sentence on controlled entry is the authority for the post-regain target.

existingKnowledge.what: The build-out scoring condition (controlled arrival beyond the initial pressure or progression line; a long clearance does not count) applies only to build-out episodes.
existingKnowledge.note: Carried by the engine since 15 October 2026; with no transition that can begin a build-out episode the build refused at structure (GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE) until stage K5 (15 October 2026): the provisional realization's start, after-score and coach-judged restarts now begin the build-out episode, and the begin condition is typed (ruling C58).

existingKnowledge.what: Play continues after a change of possession, and a regain begins a new episode.

Pressure is bounded on both sides: the building team has stability enough to organize, and established coordinated high pressure does not become the dominant identity without the context passing to RPC-002.
Several progression routes stay available (at least two).
Goalkeeper involvement is typical but not independently defining.
The coach's player count and playing area reach the game unchanged, and a count that cannot be split is refused with a sentence.
existingKnowledge.note: SD-55: session-supplied values must survive into the resolved record. The refusal of a count that cannot be split is the engine's own roster check, measured. Until the stage H3 review (15 October 2026) this entry cited SD-33, the engine's report-only rule, which does not say either.

existingKnowledge.what: Equal outfield numbers (the possession game, GF2-14.b) remain the alternative allocation, in force wherever no knowledge-authorized realization authors the counts per team.
sources: contract item GF2-14.b (OWNER_RULING, ruling C31b, 1 October 2026)

It read 'Equal outfield numbers are the only allocation current knowledge authorizes.' until then.

existingKnowledge.what: The origin of a build-out needs no further value.
existingKnowledge.note: Recorded 15 October 2026 (stage K1) as RPC-001's own statement, qualified NO_FURTHER_VALUE - the first of his three states (M6) - so the field is valid and is never filled. It was capability M6 in this record's gaps; RPC-001-18.a::V6 is no longer a stop. Canonical context knowledge on his ruling, not a provisional choice. The wording of this line is ours.

existingKnowledge.what: Controlled arrival and the long-clearance exclusion are judged against the target the scoring team attacks, within the build-out episode; a longer pass received under control is not excluded.
existingKnowledge.note: Recorded 15 October 2026 (stage K1): the two referents typed as the objective reference of the scoring team, scoped to the build-out episode (C52), with his M8 safeguard beside the exclusion (RPC-001-19.b). It was capability M8 in this record's gaps; RPC-001-18.f::V5 and 19.a::V5 are no longer stops. 'The target the scoring team attacks' is our M8 wording, which he approved; it is not his sentence.

existingKnowledge.what: A build-out episode begins with a restart taken by the goalkeeper or as a controlled defensive restart; an ordinary restart does not begin one.
existingKnowledge.note: Recorded 15 October 2026 (stage K5): his acknowledgement of our wording, "A restart, taken by the goalkeeper or as a controlled defensive restart, that begins a build-out episode.", typed as the origin's referent (register V5 version 3) and decided by GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE: a transition begins a build-out episode where it stops and restarts play, begins an episode and is taken by the goalkeeper; a controlled defensive restart is not built (no row carries a restart kind), and nothing is read as one. Canonical context knowledge on his ruling, not a provisional choice; separate from the origin needing no further value (C55), as he said. The wording of this line is ours.

gaps.description: When the building team reaches its progression target under control, does play stop (a score) or continue?
How the teams exchange roles: after a block (the coach deciding when, ends kept) or after every episode.

Where the two targets sit: the building team's progression target (placed relative to the pressure, or a prototype edge; may it sit at or short of halfway?) and the depth of the pressing team's post-regain area.
The defenders' starting arrangement: left to the coach, a relationship he authors, or a value he authors; measured from what; re-established at each build-out episode or not.
Restarts: what concludes an episode, where a build-out restarts, who restarts after a score inside a block, and what 'from the feet' means.

Allocation and goalkeepers: equal outfield numbers with the asymmetry carried by roles and targets, or unequal numbers; whether the game form's silence supports two goalkeepers; what a team's goalkeeper does while it presses.

For acknowledgement (his 9.6, revised by us): the pressing team's objective is its post-regain area, live throughout its block, with no build-out start of its own, named as the team assigned to that end.
Role exchange by block: the building and pressing roles assigned to the two teams for a block, apart from the fixed ends, with a size per block for each team's target.
Facts that differ by team (his 20 September designation rule), or the narrower form: each team's goalkeeper supplied from the chosen restart.
Starts and restarts built from the knowledge: the goalkeeper or a controlled restart, the coach choosing the location, the method recorded per activity.
gaps.note: Would also move GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE, a stop at structure.

gaps.description: One coach-judged 'episode concluded' event, in his words.
A starting placement for a team, built and stated to the coach (optionally re-established at restarts).
Only if D3 calls for it: a target placed beyond the pressure reference, and his word on halfway.

excluded.ruling: Approved. Please leave Wide Zone Advantage out of this initial Play Out from the Back demonstration. Width may be a useful environmental manipulation, but its inclusion should be justified by the intended affordances and the activity's actual conditions, not merely by its presence in a candidate list.
The Pass Combination Gate remains excluded under our previous decision.

words: The coach should also be able to change the numerical relationship when the activity warrants it.
These are different environmental manipulations, with different consequences.
Neither adjustment should be automatically mapped to Comfortable, Stretch, or Demanding.
For now, I am asking that these remain possible, authorized adjustments—not that we implement a live challenge-regulation system.

manipulations.statusBasis: His 16 October reply, item 3: 'For the first activity, I favor allowing immediate pressing from a representative starting arrangement, with starting positions and distances used to regulate the challenge.' 'I do not favor a timed release.' 'However, please do not automatically add a high-regain bonus.'
manipulations.note: Immediate pressing needs no mechanism: nothing in the game restricts when the opposition may press (RPC-001 declares S4 access, V11 and V23-V26 NON_CLAIMED and V25 NOT_AUTHORED). A designated pressure line and release when the goalkeeper plays the ball are kept as potential realizations only, and not built (item 3). No existing knowledge authorizes a high-regain incentive, and none is added. The starting arrangement that regulates the challenge is the defending team's starting relationship above (D4, M5). Nothing yet tells the coach that pressing may begin immediately: the renderer states no NON_CLAIMED declaration. Until 15 October 2026 (stage H3) this was MISSING_KNOWLEDGE; his item 3 answers it.
